data.title: What's the difference between named functions and arrow functions in JavaScript?
data.author: jrsinclair
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了JavaScript中普通函数和箭头函数的区别。普通函数有三种创建方式：函数声明、函数表达式（可以是匿名或命名函数表达式）和箭头函数。

1. **函数声明**：如`function isVowel(chr) {}`，会被JavaScript引擎提升（hoisted），在整个作用域内可用。
2. **函数表达式**：如`const takeWhile = function ...`，可以是匿名或命名函数，但命名函数的名称不会绑定到作用域，仅在错误追踪时有用。
3. **箭头函数**：如`const dropWhile = (predicate, arr) => {...}`，总是匿名且为表达式，不能直接命名，但可以被引擎推断名称。

箭头函数简洁，但与普通函数不同，没有自己的`this`、`arguments`对象，也不能用作构造函数。选择哪种函数语法取决于具体需求和上下文。

本文讨论了JavaScript中普通函数和箭头函数的区别。普通函数有三种创建方式：函数声明、函数表达式（可以是匿名或命名函数表达式）和箭头函数。

1. **函数声明**：如`function isVowel(chr) {}`，会被JavaScript引擎提升（hoisted），在整个作用域内可用。
2. **函数表达式**：如`const takeWhile = function ...`，可以是匿名或命名函数，但命名函数的名称不会绑定到作用域，仅在错误追踪时有用。
3. **箭头函数**：如`const dropWhile = (predicate, arr) => {...}`，总是匿名且为表达式，不能直接命名，但可以被引擎推断名称。

箭头函数简洁，但与普通函数不同，没有自己的`this`、`arguments`对象，也不能用作构造函数。选择哪种函数语法取决于具体需求和上下文。

data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 2025年7月，加州一陪审团裁定谷歌需向该州安卓手机用户支付3.146亿美元，因其在设备闲置时未经许可传输数据，用于定向广告等目的。原告方律师称，这给用户带来了不可避免的负担。谷歌发言人表示将上诉，称数据传输对安卓设备的安全和性能至关重要。原告于2019年提起集体诉讼，代表约1400万加州用户。另一类似诉讼将在2026年审判，涉及其他49州用户。

Jury says Google must pay California Android smartphone users $314.6m
Alphabet’s company found liable for making data transfers without permission while devices were idle
Reuters
Tue 1 Jul 2025 19.53 EDT
Last modified on Wed 2 Jul 2025 15.45 EDT
Share
A jury in San Jose, California, said on Tuesday that
Google
misused customers’ cellphone data and must pay more than $314.6m to Android smartphone users in the state, according to an attorney for the plaintiffs.
The jury agreed with the plaintiffs that
Alphabet
’s Google was liable for sending and receiving information from the devices without permission while they were idle, causing what the lawsuit had called “mandatory and unavoidable burdens shouldered by Android device users for Google’s benefit”.
A
Google
spokesperson, Jose Castaneda, said in a statement that the company would appeal, and that the verdict “misunderstands services that are critical to the security, performance, and reliability of Android devices”.
Google’s emissions up 51% as AI electricity demand derails efforts to go green
Read more
The plaintiffs’ attorney Glen Summers said the verdict “forcefully vindicates the merits of this case and reflects the seriousness of Google’s misconduct”.
The plaintiffs filed the class action in state court in 2019 on behalf of an estimated 14 million Californians. They argued that Google collected information from idle phones running its Android operating system for company uses such as targeted advertising, consuming Android users’ cellular data at their expense.
Google told the court that no Android users were harmed by the data transfers and that users consented to them in the company’s terms of service and privacy policies.
Another group filed a separate lawsuit in federal court in San Jose, bringing the same claims against Google on behalf of Android users in the other 49 states. That case is scheduled for trial in April 2026.

data.title: HN Slop: AI startup ideas generated from Hacker News
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI生成 startup 创意想法的讨论，包括功能建议、具体创意评价以及对AI生成内容的反思。

不同观点：
• **wanderingstan** 提出功能请求，希望增加选择年份的选项，以便从不同年代（如web 2或加密热潮时代）获取复古的创业想法。
• **Bjartr** 提出了 "DocuQuest" 的创意，一个利用大语言模型（LLM）将复杂技术文档转化为互动学习体验的平台，并指出当前技术文档在参考、解释和教程方面的不平衡。
• **amelius** 认为这些创意不如 https://www.halfbakery.com/ 有趣，因为后者创意来自真人，更有趣。
• **jmknoll** 赞同 "DocuQuest" 是一个好主意，认为它有实际价值。
• **trevor-e** 提出了 "SciDigest" 的创意，一个将复杂科研成果转化为大众可理解内容的平台，认为这有助于解决科研人员在解释和推广方面的难题。
• **davidjhall** 认为很多创意带有当前流行趋势的偏见（如LLM），希望有一个过滤器来筛选掉这些流行元素。
• **mittermayr** 建议将创意与 https://comsensei.com 连接，为每个创意获取可用的域名。
• **unleaded** 怀念AI生成随机有趣内容的时期，认为现代AI由于RLHF（人类反馈强化学习）和模型对齐问题，不再能生成类似内容，并希望看到GPT-2在这方面的表现。
• **anitil** 提供了一个离线解决方案，使用python生成随机创意。
• **ForgotMyUUID** 提出了 "Biomech Innovations" 的创意，一个结合基因算法、AI和秘密管理平台的穿戴设备公司，并提到习惯使用Hacker News内置搜索引擎。
• **redsparrow** 提出了一个有趣但不太实际的创意 "SwearySkyscraper"，开发个性化脏话以帮助人们应对疼痛，并将其集成到建筑减震系统中。
• **butz** 分享了 "Graphene Labs" 的创意，一个去中心化、开源的互动数据可视化和基础设施图表平台。
• **jpl56** 提出了 "Ideascope" 的创意，一个通过分析Hacker News和其他技术社区实时趋势和数据生成个性化创业想法的平台。
• **keyle** 认为这些创意很有趣，甚至不会惊讶于在Hacker News上看到类似的想法。

补充讨论：
• 创意质量和实际可行性是讨论的焦点之一，部分用户如 **amelius** 认为AI生成的创意不如人类创意有趣，而 **jmknoll** 和 **trevor-e** 则认为某些创意具有实际应用价值。
• **davidjhall** 提出了对流行趋势偏见的担忧，建议增加过滤器以筛选掉这些元素，而 **unleaded** 则怀念AI生成更随机和有趣内容的时期。
• 部分用户如 **mittermayr** 和 **butz** 提供了扩展或离线解决方案，以增强创意生成过程。
• 总体来看，用户对AI生成创意持不同态度，有的认为有趣且有潜力，有的则认为存在偏见或缺乏创新。

data.title: Hundreds of Brother printer models have an unpatchable security flaw
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 数百款Brother打印机型号存在严重安全漏洞，其中一些无法通过固件修复。安全公司Rapid7发现了八个漏洞，其中一个（CVE-2024-51978）尤为严重，攻击者可利用打印机序列号生成默认管理员密码，进而利用其他漏洞，包括获取敏感信息、崩溃设备、执行任意HTTP请求等。虽然七个漏洞可通过固件更新修复，但CVE-2024-51978需要通过更改制造工艺解决。建议用户更改默认密码以保护设备安全。

News
Hundreds of Brother printer models have an unpatchable security flaw
PSA: Remember to change the manufacturer’s default passwords on your devices.
PSA: Remember to change the manufacturer’s default passwords on your devices.
by
Jess Weatherbed
Jun 30, 2025, 10:20 AM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: Brother
Jess Weatherbed
is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.
Serious security flaws have been found in hundreds of Brother printer models that could allow attackers to remotely access devices that are still using default passwords. Eight new vulnerabilities, one of which cannot be fixed by patching the firmware, were discovered in 689 kinds of Brother home and enterprise printers by
security company Rapid7
.
The flaws also impact 59 printer models from Fujifilm, Toshiba, Ricoh, and Konica Minolta, but not every vulnerability is found on every printer model. Most of the models impacted are made by Brother, a popular home and office printer provider that
The Verge
has recommended to our readers
. If you own a Brother printer, you can check to
see if your model is affected here
.
The most serious security flaw, tracked under
CVE-2024-51978 in the National Vulnerability Database
, has a
9.8 “Critical” CVSS rating
and allows attackers to generate the device’s default admin password if they know the serial number of the printer they’re targeting. This allows attackers to exploit the other seven vulnerabilities discovered by Rapid7, which include retrieving sensitive information, crashing the device, opening TCP connections, performing arbitrary HTTP requests, and exposing passwords for connected network services.
While seven of these security flaws can be fixed via
firmware updates detailed in Rapid7’s report
, Brother indicated to the company that CVE-2024-51978 itself “cannot be fully remediated in firmware,” and will be fixed via a change to the manufacturing process for future versions of affected printer models. For current models, Brother recommends that users change the default admin password for their printer via
the device’s Web-Based Management menu
Changing default manufacturing passwords is something we should all be doing when we take a new device home anyway, and these printer vulnerabilities are a good example as to why.

• **技术与迁移问题**：
  - janmo和mtmail分享了他们的经验，指出Stripe在迁移过程中的问题，例如缺乏迁移工具和发票更正功能，导致B2B使用场景中的困难。
  - matthewtse描述了一次复杂的跨国账户迁移，指出他们没有找到高质可靠的服务提供商，最终自行解决了问题。

  - Horffupolde质疑Stripe是否允许此类迁移服务。

• **语言与拼写**：

争议焦点：
- 服务定价与市场定位之间的矛盾。
- 技术实现中的迁移困难与法律合规、隐私保护之间的平衡。
- 服务名称与潜在法律风险。

data.author: haywirez
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了图论在电子游戏中的应用。演讲者Clara Nguyễn详细讲解了图论的基本概念及其在游戏开发中的实际运用，包括3D图形中的顶点和边、赛车游戏中的圈数计算、迷宫生成及并查集（Disjoint-Sets）的应用、以及bitDP理论等。她还讨论了1982年Atari 2600游戏《Entombed》中的一个未解问题。文章强调了图论不仅限于理论研究，还在计算机图形学中有广泛的实际应用，例如三角形绘图、坐标系统、以及背面剔除（Back-Face Culling）等技术。演讲内容深入且详尽，适合对图论和游戏开发感兴趣的听众。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图论在实际应用中的使用，特别是其在电子游戏开发中的潜在和实际应用。

不同观点：
• j2kun认为，文章标题和介绍具有误导性。虽然图论确实在现实中有应用，但文章中提到的很多概念似乎是作者的假设，而非实际被游戏设计师使用的技术。他肯定了文章的创意，但指出缺乏实际应用的证据。
• Llamamoe指出，文章忽略了图语法（graph grammar）在关卡生成中的应用，特别是由游戏Unexplored首创的算法，并认为这是非常吸引人的程序生成算法。

Talk #5										-
Graph Theory Applications in Video Games
Description:
A detailed look at Graph Theory and how it can be applied to video games.
Slogan:
There's more to this than you think...
Presenters:
Clara Nguyễn
Type:

Date Originally Presented:

Talk Summary & Table of Contents
Graph Theory isn't just a topic that is restricted to being
"theory". There are several real-life applications of it. One of
those just happens to be video games. In this talk, I go over a
brief overview of several concepts where Graph Theory is applied.
The topics covered vary a bit:
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
-
Vertices in 3D space, how they are represented, and the
"rules" of dealing with vertices and edges.
Race Games & Lap Counting
-
Racing games where circuits are used to count laps, as
well as a mention of
Mario Kart Wii
and its Ultra-Shortcuts, to encourage
the simplicity of Hamiltonian Circuit checking for lap
counting.
Maze Generation w/ Disjoint-Sets & Union-Find
-
I talk about how to generate mazes efficiently, as well as
taking it a step up. Generation of multiple connected mazes
along with multi-floor/dimensional mazes are described. The
true power of the Disjoint-Set data structure with
optimisations is also discussed in depth.
bitDP, a theoretical approach
-
As a bonus, a theoretical "Part 2" to
my bitDP talk
is
included too. I talk about the theory behind it and how it
can be applied to a game to optimally guarantee that a
Hamiltonian Path exists in a generated graph.
Entombed (1982 Atari 2600 game)
-
For an added bonus, I also discuss an unsolved problem
involving an Atari 2600 game,
Entombed
.
Just a heads up, this talk is
60-75 minutes long
. Concepts
will be discussed in great depth. However, the talk was
intentionally constructed for me to be over-prepared, with topics
that can be skipped if I do not have time to cover everything. As
such, I link to this page in the slides if anyone is interested in
the full talk. Audience interaction is welcome mid-talk. In the
event that I skip topics, the questions below are guaranteed to be
covered while I'm talking.
Questions
As a requirement, we had to put questions in for the audience to
answer on paper mid-talk. The answers were hidden in the slides to
see if students were paying attention. Here are mine, with answers
at the end of the page:
Given a 3D model
M
of
n
vertices, how many triangles are drawn if done via
Triangle List
?
What is lg
*
(2
2
65536
)? Alternatively, what is the lg
*
(
6
2)?
What does bitDP stand for?
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
Most graphs discussed in our Graph Theory are abstract and may be
visualised in any way as long as it follows a set of rules.
Likewise, in computer graphics, there are "rules" too. However,
they are quite different from the theoretical graph theory we are
used to discussing. How a vertex and an edge are percived are
different and absolute.
Here's a few rules:
Vertices have
positional
coordinates (x, y, z) to
define position in space. Consequently, this means that
there is only
one
way to represent them in space.
Edges (connections between vertices) are
implied
,
based on a drawing mode of the programmer's choice. They
all have their own advantages and disadvantages. I'll
go over them below.
Everything is oriented around
triangles
. Period. If
you wanted to make a square, you do it with two triangles.
If you wanted to make a curved surface, you have to
estimate it with triangles.
Coordinate Systems
We have three dimensions to work with here. The coordinates are
cartesian, and denoted with (x, y, z). Depending on implementation,
you may find the "y" axis being the "height" axis, or the "z" axis
being the "height" axis. For simplicity of this talk, any potential
discussion of 3D coordinates will assume "z" as the "height" axis.
This is shown as follows:
Z-axis being shown as the "height" axis.
Back-Face Culling
When we draw a triangle, it's filled, obviously. However, only one
side of the triangle is drawn. The other side is invisible. This is
due to
Back-Face Culling
. The side that gets drawn depends
on the order the vertices are facing when you draw to the screen.

data.title: Peasant Railgun
data.author: cainxinth
data.article_summary: 《Peasant Railgun》是一篇介绍在《龙与地下城》桌游中一种理论战术的文章。这种战术源于2008年金融危机末期1d4chan社区的一个帖子，分为支持和反对两派。简单来说，玩家可以雇佣2280个农民站成一排，通过传递拆卸下来的长梯，在一回合内造成300d6点伤害。该战术利用了“准备动作”、“每回合时间”和“坠落物规则”等游戏机制。根据规则，长梯能在6秒内传递11400英尺，相当于时速1900英里，造成巨大伤害。然而，这种战术仅在规则上可行，现实中由于农民的脆弱和极高速度的不可操作性，实际操作中会遇到许多问题。文章最后提醒玩家，在尝试这种战术前需考虑现实物理和游戏规则的差异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于DnD中的“农民电磁炮”（Peasant Railgun）和其他类似利用规则漏洞进行横向问题解决的讨论，涉及到规则解释、游戏风格以及DM裁定权的使用。

不同观点：
• **支持创意玩法**：disillusionist承认这种玩法的趣味性，认为 lateral problem solving 是DnD体验的一部分，但指出这种玩法往往依赖于对规则的扭曲解释，不完全符合RAW（规则文字）或RAI（规则意图）。如果DM鼓励这种玩法，那完全没问题。
• **反对或限制玩法**：
  ◦ **规则局限性**：ticulatedspline和rtkwe指出这种玩法试图将现实物理与游戏机制混合，只选择对玩家有利的部分，而忽略了规则本身的限制。
  ◦ **DM的裁定权**：Ekaros和generalizations认为DM应该介入并设定限制，例如要求难度递增的掷骰或直接判定失败，以防止这种玩法破坏游戏平衡。
  ◦ **现实后果**：bovermyer强调如果允许这种战术，玩家也必须面对严重的后果，包括道德和敌对势力的反击。

• **玩家类型差异**：noelwelsh将玩家分为min-maxers和storytellers两类，前者追求规则最大化，后者则更关注故事。noelwelsh个人更倾向于故事驱动，但对不同玩家需求的平衡是RPG的一大挑战。

• **幽默与跨界**：Yizahi推荐了一部结合了DnD规则的哈利波特同人小说，体现了对这种玩法的幽默欣赏。

• **历史版本与类似战术**：kibwen和greesil提到在早期版本中也有类似战术（如鸡群战术），并分享了自己在其他游戏中类似的经验。

补充讨论：
• **游戏设计意图**：评论中多次提到DnD规则的设计并非模拟现实，而是为DM提供一个框架来协调和仲裁游戏。disillusionist和ourmandave指出官方也支持这种观点。
• **敌对势力资源**：pavel_lishin提醒DM，如果玩家能使用这种战术，那么敌对势力也可能拥有更多资源来反击玩家。

争议焦点：
• **规则解释的界限**：玩家和DM之间对于规则的解释和应用存在分歧，尤其是在如何平衡趣味性与游戏平衡方面。
• **游戏风格的兼容性**：不同玩家对游戏风格的偏好可能导致冲突，需要DM进行有效的协调和裁定。

Peasants Celebrating Twelfth Night
by David Teniers the Younger, oil on canvas.
You may have been scrolling through the
r/dnd
or
r/dndmemes
subreddits when you scrolled past a comment containing the phrase “
Peasant Railgun”
, and if you were like me, instantly became confused. So my dear and sweet reader, I have taken it upon myself to find the answer to the question: What is a Peasant Railgun?
What is the Peasant Railgun?
During the tail-end of the 2008 financial crisis,
1d4chan
released a post detailing a theory that they had been working on. When released, two sides erupted from within the community; DM’s who had enough, and players who begged their DM to allow it.
In summary, the party could hypothetically hire 2,280 peasants, have them stand in a line, and have them do 300d6  damage by throwing a dismantled ladder at your foes. The best part? This process only takes one round of combat, and can be reloaded and fired again in less than 12 seconds.

How does the Peasant Railgun work?
Several different rules come into play to achieve this. The Ready Action, the Amount of Time it takes to takes to complete one round of combat, space taken up by any one medium-sized individual, and
Falling Object rules
for 5e.
The Ready action is meant for when a player wants to get the jump on a foe or wait for a particular circumstance. To do this, the Ready action allows you to act using your reaction before the start of your next turn. You might already see where this is heading… but I continue.
When taking the Ready action, the player establishes a circumstance that will trigger the reaction. In this case, you disassemble the ladder and give the wooden pole to the person at the end of the line. You then direct everyone to ready their action to pass the pole to the peasant in front of them. After that, you then run to the front and tell the peasant to aim at the BBEG, stone castle, or any poor soul that dares stand in your way.
At the start of combat, the chain of events is initiated and that wooden rod is carried two miles in
6 seconds
which means it had to accelerate to the speed of 1900 miles per hour. This is due in part that a medium creature (which human peasants categorize as) takes up a one-by-one 5 foot square. Multiply that space times 2,280, and you easily get a line that spans two miles.
Peasant Line Length
: 5ft x 2,280 individuals= 11,400ft
Time Per Round of Combat
: 6 seconds
Miles Per Hour:
11,400ft/6seconds= 1188mph*
Falling Object Rule
: (11,400ft/60ft)/ 2d6= 300d6**
This is also possible due to there being no restrictions on how many combatants can participate in combat, and how long a single round takes. Combine the fact that a single round encompasses the action economy of every single individual involved, than you get a really,
really
, fast rod.
Lastly, the Peasant Railgun takes into account the Falling Object rule which assumes the wooden pole weighs 7 pounds and would do 2d6 damage per 60ft. Do the math and you end up with our 300d6 of damage per turn!
Real Life Physics vs. RAW
Now before you send this article to your DM saying “I have an idea for next session…” there are a couple of things you should probably consider first.
Everything we have discussed so far is possible under rules as written (RAW) which don’t entirely adhere to real life physics (which is probably why you haven’t seen the military take advantage of the Peasant Railgun quite yet). If we were to take this quite literally, you’d see problems arise quite quickly.
Peasant Stat Block
One of the major problems would be the absolute destruction caused to those you convinced to line up for this weird tango. If a wooden rod was going at that speed, as it accelerates (which RAW doesn’t even account for), those peasants who would grab the rod would most likely have to roll to see if they could even withstand the pain of encountering an object at that speed. The 4 (1d8 average) hit points assigned to the
commoner stat block
would probably not leave many of our 2,280 peasants left standing.
The second problem is that most people can’t track an item going at that speed, let alone pass it to the person in front of them. When you gather for your next session, grab a tennis bal
44455222.article_summary: 《Peasant Railgun》是一篇介绍在《龙与地下城》桌游中一种理论战术的文章。这种战术源于2008年金融危机末期1d4chan社区的一个帖子，分为支持和反对两派。简单来说，玩家可以雇佣2280个农民站成一排，通过传递拆卸下来的长梯，在一回合内造成300d6点伤害。该战术利用了“准备动作”、“每回合时间”和“坠落物规则”等游戏机制。根据规则，长梯能在6秒内传递11400英尺，相当于时速1900英里，造成巨大伤害。然而，这种战术仅在规则上可行，现实中由于农民的脆弱和极高速度的不可操作性，实际操作中会遇到许多问题。文章最后提醒玩家，在尝试这种战术前需考虑现实物理和游戏规则的差异。
44455222.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于DnD中的“农民电磁炮”（Peasant Railgun）和其他类似利用规则漏洞进行横向问题解决的讨论，涉及到规则解释、游戏风格以及DM裁定权的使用。

不同观点：
• **支持创意玩法**：disillusionist承认这种玩法的趣味性，认为 lateral problem solving 是DnD体验的一部分，但指出这种玩法往往依赖于对规则的扭曲解释，不完全符合RAW（规则文字）或RAI（规则意图）。如果DM鼓励这种玩法，那完全没问题。
• **反对或限制玩法**：
  ◦ **规则局限性**：ticulatedspline和rtkwe指出这种玩法试图将现实物理与游戏机制混合，只选择对玩家有利的部分，而忽略了规则本身的限制。
  ◦ **DM的裁定权**：Ekaros和generalizations认为DM应该介入并设定限制，例如要求难度递增的掷骰或直接判定失败，以防止这种玩法破坏游戏平衡。
  ◦ **现实后果**：bovermyer强调如果允许这种战术，玩家也必须面对严重的后果，包括道德和敌对势力的反击。

• **玩家类型差异**：noelwelsh将玩家分为min-maxers和storytellers两类，前者追求规则最大化，后者则更关注故事。noelwelsh个人更倾向于故事驱动，但对不同玩家需求的平衡是RPG的一大挑战。

• **幽默与跨界**：Yizahi推荐了一部结合了DnD规则的哈利波特同人小说，体现了对这种玩法的幽默欣赏。

• **历史版本与类似战术**：kibwen和greesil提到在早期版本中也有类似战术（如鸡群战术），并分享了自己在其他游戏中类似的经验。

补充讨论：
• **游戏设计意图**：评论中多次提到DnD规则的设计并非模拟现实，而是为DM提供一个框架来协调和仲裁游戏。disillusionist和ourmandave指出官方也支持这种观点。
• **敌对势力资源**：pavel_lishin提醒DM，如果玩家能使用这种战术，那么敌对势力也可能拥有更多资源来反击玩家。

争议焦点：
• **规则解释的界限**：玩家和DM之间对于规则的解释和应用存在分歧，尤其是在如何平衡趣味性与游戏平衡方面。
• **游戏风格的兼容性**：不同玩家对游戏风格的偏好可能导致冲突，需要DM进行有效的协调和裁定。

Title:
Alice's Adventures in a Differentiable Wonderland -- Volume I, A Tour of the Land
Authors:
Simone Scardapane
View a PDF of the paper titled Alice's Adventures in a Differentiable Wonderland -- Volume I, A Tour of the Land, by Simone Scardapane
View PDF
Abstract:
Neural networks surround us, in the form of large language models, speech transcription systems, molecular discovery algorithms, robotics, and much more. Stripped of anything else, neural networks are compositions of differentiable primitives, and studying them means learning how to program and how to interact with these models, a particular example of what is called differentiable programming.
This primer is an introduction to this fascinating field imagined for someone, like Alice, who has just ventured into this strange differentiable wonderland. I overview the basics of optimizing a function via automatic differentiation, and a selection of the most common designs for handling sequences, graphs, texts, and audios. The focus is on a intuitive, self-contained introduction to the most important design techniques, including convolutional, attentional, and recurrent blocks, hoping to bridge the gap between theory and code (PyTorch and JAX) and leaving the reader capable of understanding some of the most advanced models out there, such as large language models (LLMs) and multimodal architectures.

data.title: Show HN: HomeBrew HN – Generate personal context for content ranking
data.author: azath92
data.article_summary: HomeBrew HN 是一个由 Leo、Lewis 和 Steffan 在伦敦开发的平台。用户可以通过点击 "Get Recommendations" 获取个性化的 Hacker News (HN) 帖子推荐。此外，用户还可以刷新帖子列表和编辑个人资料。该平台旨在提升 Hacker News 内容浏览的个性化和便捷性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人兴趣档案生成工具的评价与改进建议

不同观点：
• 支持与赞赏：  
  - gwintrob和drakonka对工具的整体设计表示赞赏，尤其是将个人档案以Markdown形式展示，并认为此工具很有创意和实用性。
  - huem0n认为该工具的界面设计（如颜色和UI）合理，且对于初步原型表示肯定，期待其持续学习和改进。
  - bstsb对工具从少量数据中准确总结个人兴趣表示惊讶，并对生成的个人档案感到满意。

• 对工具改进的建议：  
  - huem0n和mdrzn建议工具应结合用户的点赞和评论历史来生成更准确的兴趣档案。
  - pxc指出，对于小众兴趣用户，当前基于近期热门文章的采样方法不够有效，建议用户可以手动输入兴趣关键词以提高准确性，并建议工具分析文章内容而不仅是标题。
  - password4321提出，用户的点赞历史和评论可以作为公开信号用于改进推荐。

• 对推荐准确性的反馈：  
  - NitpickLawyer认为工具对他的技术兴趣分析相当准确，但希望可以与自己评论过的主题进行对比。
  - pxc则指出工具对他的兴趣分析有误，特别是在低层次技术细节和理论计算机科学方面的兴趣评估不准确。

• 其他功能与技术讨论：  
  - peterm4希望工具能整合对HN评论的兴趣分析，而不仅是文章本身。
  - mebazaa询问是否考虑过使用传统的推荐系统，并结合LLM生成合成偏好。
  - wasabi991011对如何评估文章（基于标题还是内容）提出疑问。
  - flexagoon幽默地表示自己的兴趣其实只与有趣的标题有关，而非文章内容。
  - simongray则感慨HN平台上LLM内容的泛滥。

补充讨论：
• wickedsight对工具的技术架构感兴趣，并希望了解更多技术细节，表明该工具在技术社区引起了专业兴趣。
• 整体上，评论中有多个用户对工具的个性化和持续学习能力提出了期望，并提供了具体改进建议。

data.author: bryanrasmussen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对斯蒂芬·马拉美诗歌《骰子一掷永远取消不了偶然》中核心思想的解读及其应用

不同观点：
• Dropbysometime认为该诗歌表达了“偶然性无法被消除”的观点。他解释道，即使在艺术创作或人生历程中，偶然性可以作为一种催化剂或灵感来源，但其本质是无法被控制或消除的。他引用了诗歌中的“掷骰子”作为代表偶然和不可预测性的象征，并提到诗歌试图捕捉绝对性但失败了，反映了人类在控制偶然性方面的无力。他还指出，这首诗因其创新的排版和思想成为现代主义诗歌的奠基之作，强调了人类控制的局限性和偶然性的力量。最后，他以幽默的方式提到程序员对待生活和偶然性的态度。

• VinLucero从另一个角度出发，认为这首诗体现了智慧高于智力的价值，以及在任何时候成为通才而非专才的重要性。这一观点将诗歌的思想引申到了个人发展和生活哲学的层面，强调了广泛涉猎和灵活应对偶然性的重要性。

• Dropbysometime提出了一个实际问题，即在偶然性（如运气好坏）对人生路径有重要影响的情况下，如何过上幸福生活（路径依赖问题）。这引发了对如何在不可控因素影响下寻求幸福和满足的思考。

data.title: Locality of Behaviour (2020)
data.author: jstanley
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了**行为局部性（LoB）**原则，强调代码单元的行为应尽可能直观，以便于理解和维护。作者引用Richard Gabriel的观点，指出良好的代码应让程序员通过查看少量代码即可理解其行为。文章对比了使用htmx和jQuery实现AJAX请求的例子，前者行为明显直观，符合LoB原则，而后者行为分散，不易理解。LoB与**DRY（不重复自己）**和**SoC（关注点分离）**等其他原则可能产生冲突，开发者需根据具体情况做出权衡。总体而言，遵循LoB原则有助于提高软件的可维护性、质量和可持续性。

Locality of Behaviour (LoB)
Carson Gross
May 29, 2020
“The primary feature for easy maintenance is locality: Locality is that characteristic of source code that enables a
programmer to understand that source by looking at only a small portion of it.” –
Richard Gabriel
The LoB Principle
Locality of Behaviour is the principle that:
The behaviour of a unit of code should be as obvious as possible by looking only at that unit of code
Discussion
The LoB principle is a simple prescriptive formulation of the quoted statement from
Richard Gabriel
.
In as much as it is possible, and in balance with other concerns, developers should strive to make the behaviour of
a code element obvious on inspection.
Consider two different implementations of an AJAX request in HTML, the first in
htmx
:
<
button
hx-get
=
"/clicked"
>Click Me</
button
>
and the second in
jQuery
:
$
(
"#d1"
).
on
(
"click"
,
function
(){
$
.
ajax
({
/* AJAX options... */
});
});
<
button
id
=
"d1"
>Click Me</
button
>
In the former, the behaviour of the
button
element is obvious on inspection, satisfying the LoB principle.
In the latter, the behaviour of the
button
element is spread out amongst multiple files.  It is difficult to know
exactly what the button does without a total knowledge of the code base.  This “spooky action at a distance” is a source
of maintenance issues and stands in the way of developers understanding of the code base.
The htmx example demonstrates good Locality of Behaviour, while the jQuery example has poor Locality of Behaviour.
Surfacing Behaviour vs. Inlining Implementation
A common objection to Locality of Behaviour is that it is inlining implementation details within a code unit, making the
code unit less abstract and more brittle.  However, it is important to make the distinction between inlining the
implementation
of some behaviour and inlining the invocation (or declaration) of some behaviour.
Consider functions in most programming languages: there is a distinction between the declaration of function and its
use at call sites.  A good function abstracts away its implementation details, but is also invoked in an obvious manner,
without any spooky action at a distance.
Increasing the obviousness of the behaviour of an element is, ceteris paribus, a good thing, but it falls to both end-developers
and especially framework developers to make LoB both as easy and as conceptually clean as possible.
Conflict With Other Development Principles
The LoB will often conflict with other software development principles.  Two important ones
are:
DRY - Don’t Repeat Yourself
Software developers typically strive to avoid redundancy in their code or data.  This has come to be called “Staying DRY”,
i.e. Don’t Repeat Yourself.  Like other software design principles this, on its own, is a good thing.  htmx, for example,
allows you to place many attributes on parent elements in a DOM and avoid repeating these attributes on children.  This is a
violation of LoB, in favor of DRY, and such tradeoffs need to be made judiciously by developers.
Note that the further behaviour gets from the code unit it effects, the more severe the violation of LoB.  If it is
within a few lines of the code unit, this is less serious than if it is a page away, which is less serious than if
it is in a separate file entirely.
There is no hard and fast rule, but rather subjective tradeoffs that must be made as software developers.
SoC - Separation Of Concerns
Separation of concerns a design principle for separating a computer program into distinct sections such that each
section addresses a separate concern.  A canonical example of this is splitting HTML, CSS, and Javascript.  Again, on its own and
in isolation this may, indeed, be a good thing.  Inlining styles
has become more prevalent lately
,
but there are still strong arguments in favor of SoC in this regard.
Note that SoC is, however, in conflict with LoB.  By tweaking a CSS file the look and, to an extent, behaviour of an
element can change dramatically, and it is not obvious where this dramatic change came from.  Tools can help to an extent
here, but there is still “spooky action at a distance” going on.
Again, this isn’t to condemn SoC wholesale, just to say that there are subjective tradeoffs that must be made when
considering how to structure your code.  The fact that inline styles have become more prevalent as of late is an
indication that SoC is losing some support amongst developers.
Conclusion
LoB is a subjective software design principle that can help make a code base more humane and maintainable.  It must be traded
off against other design principles and be considered in terms of the limitations of the system a code unit is
written in, but, as much as is it is practical, adherence to this principle will increase your software maintainability,
quality and sustainability.

data.title: Introducing tmux-rs
data.author: Jtsummers
data.article_summary: 作者Collin Richards介绍了将tmux从C语言移植到Rust的项目。历时六个月，他达到了一个重要里程碑：代码库现在100%由Rust编写（使用了unsafe）。原始C代码约67,000行，Rust版本则为约81,000行。作者最初使用了C2Rust工具进行自动转换，但生成代码难以维护且比原C代码大三倍。最终，作者放弃了自动转换，选择手动翻译每个文件。尽管如此，C2Rust工具仍帮助作者验证了项目的可行性。作者还详细描述了构建过程，并分享了一些有趣的bug和开发经验，如使用Vim和AI工具辅助开发。最终，项目取得了成功，展示了将复杂C项目移植到Rust的可行性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust重写tmux项目的不同观点和潜在应用

不同观点：
• [mbreese] 认为重写已有工具不需要特别理由，纯粹是爱好项目，类似于园艺活动，且指出编码比园艺更安全，避免了实际操作中的错误（如园艺中的segfaults）。
• [ethagnawl] 对Rust重写tmux表示关注，并分享了自己正在开发的Rust版tmux会话管理器rmuxinator。他考虑将tmux-rs和rmuxinator结合使用，以改进会话管理功能，但不建议将其纳入上游项目。
• [gmoque] 支持重写项目，认为这种过程能带来许多学习机会，并建议通过修复bug和优化代码吸引Rust初学者参与。他还提出了一个结合Gemini CLI和AI的创意用例。
• [uecker] 对重写成熟应用持保留态度，指出无论是自动翻译还是手动翻译，都会引入许多bug，因此不建议重写已稳定运行的代码，除非是 hobby project。
• [tekawade] 表达了对Rust的喜爱，并提到Zellij，一个基于Rust的终端复用器，认为迁移到Rust解决方案是可行的。
• [a-dub] 希望tmux支持远程连接多个后端实例，这是一个功能性期望。
• [tialaramex] 分享了一个关于Rust开发命令行工具的视频资源，认为对Rust开发者有帮助。
• [someperson] 建议改进c2rust工具以减少信息丢失和转换负担。
• [xvilka] 对Zellij不满意，认为其缺少tmux的许多功能，如显示/隐藏状态栏。
• [rthnbgrredf] 认为未来LLM有可能实现自动化代码翻译，但目前技术尚未成熟，仍需时间发展。
• [teekert] 希望tmux改进用户界面交互，如滚轮滚动和快捷键操作，尽管知道这不是合适的反馈场所。
• [df0b9f169d54] 提到tmux在内存使用上存在问题，期待Rust版本能有所改善。
• [submeta] 高度评价tmux及其会话管理功能，并期待尝试tmux-rs。
• [londons_explore] 提出LLM在代码翻译上的潜力，认为可以通过代码转换来实现代码清理，并质疑原作者为何不利用此方法作为起点。

• 争议焦点之一是重写成熟应用的必要性和价值，特别是手动翻译代码引入的bug问题。
• 另一个讨论点是Rust重写tmux的潜在功能改进，如AI结合和远程连接支持。
• 多个评论提到了Zellij和rmuxinator等类似项目，比较了它们的优缺点。
• 有人对Rust版本在性能和内存管理上的潜在改善抱有期待。
• 最后，LLM在代码翻译和清理中的应用潜力也被多次提及。

Introducing tmux-rs
by Collin Richards
For the 6 months or so I’ve been quietly porting tmux from C to Rust. I’ve recently reached a big milestone: the code base is now 100% (unsafe) Rust.
I’d like to share the process of porting the original codebase from ~67,000 lines of C code to ~81,000 lines of Rust (excluding comments and empty lines).
You might be asking: why did you rewrite tmux in Rust? And yeah, I don’t really have a good reason. It’s a hobby project. Like gardening, but with more segfaults.

return

1
as
libc

c_int
);
}
This snippet isn’t that bad, but things can get a lot worse. My main concern was losing information from named constants like
COLOUR_FLAG_256
which is translated to
0x1000000
. There are also a lot of casts to
libc::c_int
polluting the code as well. I suspect this is to handle
C’s integer promotion rules
. Most of them are completely unnecessary when doing operations on literals in Rust.
I spent quite a lot of time manually refactoring the shitty Rust code to less shitty Rust code, but I kept finding myself having to look at the original C code to understand the program’s intent. After manually refactoring many files this way I gave up on this approach. I threw away all of the C2Rust output and decided I would translate all of the files into Rust manually from C.
Despite not using C2Rust for this project I still think it’s a great tool. It was very important for me to actually be able to compile and run the project from the start. It made me realize this endeavour was achievable. I’ve even integrated it as part of one of my
other side projects

data.title: Doom Didn't Kill the Amiga (2024)
data.author: blakespot
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者作为Amiga电脑的忠实用户，回顾了Amiga的兴衰历程。作者在1988年首次接触Amiga 500，并于1992年购买了一台Amiga 500+。在当时，Amiga以其优越的图形和声音表现超越了其他家用电脑，如C64和Atari ST。尽管PC开始崭露头角，但在1992年，Amiga在性价比和游戏体验上仍具优势。然而，随着技术迅速发展，PC硬件价格下降，尤其是像《Doom》这样的游戏出现，使得PC逐渐成为强劲对手。虽然有人认为《Doom》导致了Amiga的衰落，但作者认为这只是技术发展的一个表现，而非根本原因。Commodore在硬件更新上的频繁变动和未能跟上技术潮流才是Amiga衰落的主因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amiga电脑的衰落原因及不同用户视角

不同观点：
• **个人经历视角：Amiga因游戏迁移到PC**  
  [runjake] 提到自己在1992年因为《Wolfenstein 3D》游戏从Amiga转向PC，并指出大多数朋友也已经转向其他平台。他还提到《Doom》在1993年发布，进一步加速了这一转变。

• **游戏机竞争视角：游戏机淘汰了Amiga**  
  [louthy] 认为游戏机（如家用游戏机）的兴起淘汰了Amiga等以游戏为主的家庭电脑，而PC因为用于商业用途得以幸存。他指出自己不认识任何用Amiga做非游戏用途的人。

• **地域差异视角：英国80-90年代电脑普及情况**  
  [bhlkjlkjcd] 对[louthy]的观点提出异议，基于自己在英国的经历指出，20世纪80年代末到90年代初，英国的孩子们普遍拥有各种8位和16位电脑，而非游戏机。他提到自己所在的社区大多数孩子拥有Commodore 64、Sinclair Spectrum等电脑，而非游戏机。

• **PC游戏优势视角：PC的崛起与Amiga的局限**  
  [leshokunin] 作为长期PC玩家，认为1993-1996年是PC游戏市场的巅峰期，列举了多款当时流行的PC游戏如《Day of the Tentacle》、《Myst》等，并提到PC游戏在技术和内容上的领先，使得Amiga显得不再必要。

• **Amiga的特定用途存续：专业应用延缓其消亡**  
  [mzs] 提到Amiga因特定应用（如Video Toaster）在某些领域存续了一段时间，甚至到2001年还有电视台使用Amiga系统。

• **技术局限视角：Amiga技术架构的过时**  
  [cmrdporcupine] 从技术角度分析Amiga的衰落，指出其芯片设计和内存行为导致其无法跟上技术发展，尤其是当内存和总线速度大幅提升时。他还提到Atari ST的用户体验，并认为转向486和Linux是更合理的选择。

• **Amiga产品定位争议：是否应作为游戏机推出**  
  [andrewstuart] 认为Amiga本质上是作为游戏机伪装成电脑，并提出如果Amiga一开始就作为CD32这种游戏机推出，或许公司还能存活至今。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点：Doom是否导致Amiga的衰落**  
  [ChrisArchitect] 分享了一个视频链接，认为《Wolfenstein 3D》而非《Doom》才是Amiga衰落的原因，并引发进一步讨论。

总体来看，讨论围绕Amiga电脑的衰落原因展开，涉及个人经历、地域差异、技术局限以及Amiga的产品定位等多方面因素。

how doom didn't kill the amiga
How Doom didn't kill the Amiga
A detailed account of the rise and fall of an Amiga zealot
Early 2024
A scene from the Amiga game Defender of the Crown, released in 1986.
For years, no other home computer came close to screens like these.
Ever since I saw an Amiga 500 at a friend's house in what was probably late 1988, I wanted one for myself. Back then, computers were uncommon, especially at home. Even though I went to a school in a fairly affluent neighborhood, few kids had home computers or video games.
Gradually, that started to change.
I bought my own Amiga in February 1992. It was basically the same exact model as the one I had first seen in 1988: An Amiga 500+ with a 7 MHz 68000 CPU, 1 meg of RAM, 8-bit stereo PCM sound and many various graphics modes, of which 320x256 in 16 or 32 colors was the most common for games.
Competing Platforms
Buying any other computer was completely out of the question. There were practical reasons of course: I knew how it worked and friends had one, which meant we could copy pirated games from each other. And it ran
Deluxe Paint
, an era defining graphics program and a killer application for anyone with artistic inclinations, which I'd convinced myself I had.
I had also come into contact with other types of machines. The C64 felt like a thing of the past, with blocky graphics and beepy sound. The Mac was a boring monochrome computer made for writing equally boring documents about tax deductions. I intensely remember seeing a PC for the first time, and how disappointed it made me: it was much worse than the Mac, possibly even than the C64. Downright ugly graphics, terrible sound and a mysterious operating system that required you to learn textual incantations by heart.
But the real home computer feud during those days was between the Amiga 500 and the Atari ST, in which the latter always seemed to come out losing; worse sound, worse graphics, worse OS. Such a machine was completely out of the question - it just
had
to be an Amiga.
I don't regret this decision one bit. Few gadgets have given me as much joy and positive experiences as my Amigas, and even in 1992 an Amiga 500 wasn't a bad purchase. The PC was still a fairly boring machine, having a hard time keeping up with the Amiga's sound and graphics without costing an exorbitant amount of money. The revolutionary Amiga architecture, released in 1985 and basically unchanged since then, could still hold its own: a testament to its ingenuity.
The Price is Right
Around this time, PC:s were showing signs of becoming affordable, and Amiga style platform- and arcade games had begun appearing on the platform. But even the most straightforward of these titles required a fast 386 CPU, plenty of memory and a VGA card to come close to the amount of motion and commotion the Amiga had been capable of for ages. This meant the price to play was still high: In Sweden, around Christmas 1992, a 25 MHz 386/SX with 2 megs of RAM and a 40 meg hard drive was selling for $530. To this came the additional cost of a sound card. A Sound Blaster 2.0, guaranteed to be supported by most games, was available for a whopping $129. While you could hook the Amiga to a cheap 14" TV via RGB SCART, the PC required an expensive VGA monitor, on which you couldn't also watch MacGyver. Bummer!
Shadow of the Beast, released for the Amiga in 1989. It featured
lush graphics, multiple layers of parallax scrolling, massive sprites
and tough as nails gameplay. It looked like crap on pretty much every
other system, and wasn't even ported to the then inferior PC.
This put the cost of an entry level 386 system at $660 without software, compared to the Amiga 600's $499, and the A600's 40 MB hard drive came pre-loaded with Deluxe Paint, a word processor and several decent games. It's true that a 386 PC was much faster than the 7 MHz Amiga in some aspects, but most of those aspects didn't matter for people like me and my friends - at least not yet.
More Moore
It's hard to convey just how intense the effects of Moore's law were during the 90's. When it came to hardware, December 1992 was a
very
different time compared to January 1992. During this year, Commodore pulled a stunt by first introducing the A500+ and then swiftly replacing it with the A600 - a low cost model with the advantage of having an integrated IDE interface, only to finish off by making the A600 obsolete with the release of the next-generation A1200. They were widely criticized for this, but in their defense, home computing was moving at breakneck speed and nobody could really keep up. At any given moment, something that had been unfeasible just six months ago was suddenly commonplace. One such something was
Doom
- which was nowhere, and then suddenly everywhere. Some Amiga fanatics still claim that Doom was what killed the Amiga, but I don't believe that to be true. Doom was a symptom, not the disease proper.

data.title: Where is my von Braun wheel?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了为何NASA在1962年放弃了旋转轮形空间站的研发，转而专注于阿波罗登月计划，导致人工重力空间站的设想被搁置。文章指出，这一历史性决策导致了之后长达半个世纪的小型零重力空间站的模式，给宇航员带来肌肉萎缩、骨质流失和视力问题等健康挑战。早期太空先驱如冯·布劳恩曾认为人工重力对长期太空生活至关重要，其设计的旋转轮形空间站本可实现这一目标。然而，建造大型旋转空间站面临工程挑战，需要解决如何将巨大结构装入细长火箭的难题。文章最后提到，商业航天公司如今重新考虑人工重力站的可能性，或能纠正这一历史性偏差，推动人类成为太空文明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太空探索与殖民的技术和可行性

不同观点：
• **支持充气结构和太空酒店的潜力**：  
  - [jauntywundrkind] 提到充气结构（如货船的翼帆、豪华双体船MODX、NASA的"Orbital Reef"等）是金属墙壁的明显且优秀的替代品，如果技术成功，将带来巨大的进步。  
  - 举例：NASA和Sierra Space合作测试的300立方米"Orbital Reef"，以及中国去年测试的类似结构。  

• **Starship与大型太空结构的潜力**：  
  - [PaulHoule] 认为SpaceX的Starship成功入轨后，可以构建比国际空间站（ISS）大但小于O'Neill殖民地的结构。提到Starship可以实现大型太空酒店和模拟环境，但O'Neill殖民地因需要大量氮气而不切实际。  
  - 提到太空制造的关键路径可能是结合3D打印、流动化学、合成生物学等技术。  
  - 特别指出Ceres的殖民潜力，因为水和氮充足，可能建立比地球更大的人口与空间。

• **太空殖民与人工重力的必要性**：  
  - [bryanlarsen] 强调长期零重力实验的重要性，并提出第二座空间站应考虑人工重力（通过离心力）。  
  - [abe94] 质疑为何不专注于建造大型太空结构，而是一味追求行星殖民。  
  - [dan-robertson] 反对人类大规模移居其他星球，认为政府不应为此投入大量资金，且火星任务可能破坏潜在的生命迹象。  

• **技术实现与实际限制**：  
  - [aidenn0] 提出"I"或"H"形状的系统设计，认为这样能有效增加居住面积，且不显著增加发射次数。  
  - [Someone] 质疑大规模旋转结构（如75米直径的轮子）对人体影响，特别是不同高度的重力差异。  
  - [kevin_thibedeau] 指出早期整体式空间站概念未考虑到现代微处理器、电子控制系统和紧凑机器人技术的发展，且当时没有适合发射大型结构的火箭。

Where is my von Braun wheel?
Completion: 95%
3604 words
Essay first planted: March 25, 2025 • Last updated: July 3, 2025
In 1962. There — that answers the clickbaity title right away.
NASA had viable designs for rotating wheel space stations that could have given astronauts artificial gravity. Then, the Apollo program effectively killed them.
While NASA’s lunar focus delivered the historic moonshot, it dismantled a promising engineering effort at Langley Research Center that might have revolutionized human spaceflight. That decision set us on a half-century trajectory of small, zero-gravity stations that continue to plague astronauts with
muscle atrophy
,
bone loss
, and
vision problems
.
Had NASA maintained its parallel pursuit of artificial gravity, we might now have permanent orbital settlements supporting deep space missions rather than the limited outposts we’ve settled for. This historical pivot point matters today as commercial space companies contemplate artificial gravity again, potentially correcting a costly detour in humanity’s path to becoming a spacefaring civilisation.
James Webb, the former NASA administrator immortalised by the JWST, standing underneath a prototype of a von Braun Wheel
The need for artificial gravity
Early space visionaries, such as Werner von Braun, strongly believed that settling the solar system required developing technologies to generate artificial gravity within orbiting habitats as — rephrasing
Heinlein
— space is a harsh mistress. Modern-day astronauts
exercise a few hours each day
to overcome
microgravity
’s effects on
the body
. Von Braun was convinced that rotating wheel space stations prevented such physiological problems and were thus “
as inevitable as the rising sun
”. In these systems, humans live along the periphery of a wheel, within which they experience gravity due to the wheel’s rotation. Popularised by von Braun in his 1949 sci-fi novel,
Project Mars
, and the
1956 Disney piece
, the concept actually traces back to
Herman Potočnik
’s 1929 book
The Problem of Space Travel
. Its legacy is perhaps why many felt that an operational spinning station was, at best, a couple decades away.

Potočnik’s first conceptualised the rotating space station.
von Braun explaining the layout of his wheel-shaped station
The difficulty of building large stations
⊕
Rotational forces applied to wine tasting.
This elegant solution to generate artificial gravity, however, comes with a major engineering challenge. Much like a ferris wheel, the wheel’s rotation could disorient astronauts if spun too fast. If the wheel spins slowly then its physics dictates it must be quite large. For example, one of von Braun’s designs called for a massive 75 metre diameter wheel that generated lunar gravity if spun at 3 rpm and Earth-like gravity at 5 rpm — this range is considered
reasonable for astronauts
.
However, the physics of rockets presents a different obstacle as it must be slender, like an arrow, to escape Earth’s gravity well and reach orbit. This defines the main upstream engineering challenge: how can we fit enormous space structures into slender rockets? For context, even Starship’s
upper-stage
, which is about 9 metres wide and 22 metres tall cannot fit von Braun’s conceptual station in a straightforward manner.
Architects of the International Space Station (ISS), the largest space structure ever built, tackled a similar packing problem using multiple smaller spacecraft which connect, like space Ikea, into a structure greater than its parts. Such in-space assembly involves spacecraft either gently crashing into each other at specific connection points (a manoeuvre called
rendezvous and docking
) as well as
astronauts and space cranes
supporting finer assembly tasks. While this works great in theory, the ISS’s assembly needed over 40 rocket launches spanning several years (and even more launches for cargo resupply and repairs). More damning is the typical ISS crew size of 7, which is a little over twice that of the first ever space station, Salyut, from 1972. Clearly 50 years of space station development does not indicate that such modular in-orbit assembly will scale to von Braun’s
anticipated 80 humans
or, more relevant today, Starship’s
100
any time soon. Civilisation-scale megastructures like the Stanford Torus and O’Neill cylinders appear even more outlandish to discuss today than when they were first proposed in the 70s.
The Stanford Torus concept for 10,000 space settlers was proposed during the 1975 NASA Summer Study.
The O’Neill cylinder was proposed in 1976 by Gerard O’Neill.
From this vantage point, it is quite clear that the architectural bottleneck is a technology running through all operational space stations so far: their use of small ‘tin can’ modular spacecraft as the centrepiece for assembly, which is a legacy of Apollo. This, in my opinion, is unfit

Spending Too Much Money on a Coding Agent
On making use of large thinking models.
June 30, 2025 •
7 min read
For a year, I’d been coding almost every day with Cursor and Claude Sonnet. Anthropic’s 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet each rightly earned their dominant place on the
programming model charts
: they were the least-bad coding models yet.
In the earliest days of LLMs, there was tremendous interest in ever-larger model releases. Hype around bigger, slower models has since waned, as Claude 3 Opus, GPT 4.5, and OpenAI o1 – all large and technically impressive model releases, each useful for some niche purposes – were ultimately too expensive and slow to be worth the squeeze for day-to-day coding.
But then, this spring, something interesting happened.
Full speed ahead
Last month, my co-founder Jenn and I were rapidly sprinting to hit a self-imposed deadline (demoing our latest experiment at Web Summit Vancouver). Luckily, Claude Sonnet is truly helpful when coding – especially in TypeScript. Still, under time pressure, I started to get annoyed with its LLM-isms: overcomplicating changes, proposing unnecessary dependencies, and just
literally changing failing tests into skipped tests
to resolve “the tests are failing.” Like, what the crap?
Frustrated, I tried switching from Claude Sonnet to the new o3 thinking model. I knew o3 was painfully slow, so I took the time to write out exactly what I knew, and what I wanted the solution to look like, and gave it some time to work. To my surprise, the response was… great?
The more I tried it, the more I found o3’s improved ability to use tools, assess progress, and self-correct led to results that were actually worth the wait. I found myself expanding what terminal commands I allowed the agent to run, helping it get further than ever before. When I completed a hard “o3-grade” task and moved on to something simpler, I was increasingly tempted to leave it on o3 instead of switching back. Sonnet was faster in theory. But o3 was faster in practice.
The only problem was, it was costing a fortune.
Depending on the task, my o3 conversations were averaging roughly $5 of Cursor requests each, or about $50 a day. That… is a lot of money.
Still, we were in a hurry. And what is a startup if not a series of experiments? So I turned to my co-founder.
Jenn, I have a proposal. You’re going to hate it.
I’m listening?
So you know I’ve been getting really good results from o3. I propose we try just defaulting to o3 for the next 3 weeks until our demo, and increase our Cursor spending cap to $1000/mo.
That’s a
lot
of money.
I know. It’s ridiculous. This is ridiculous. But also, when we hire a Founding Engineer, they will cost a lot more than that. Like, 10x more.
…Okay. Let’s try it. If it’s not worth the cost, we’ll go back.
So we tried it. And, to both of our horror, it was worth the cost.
We’ve found that compared to Claude 4 Sonnet and GPT-4.1, large thinking models like Claude 4 Opus and especially OpenAI o3 will:
More successfully use tools like MCPs and CLIs to troubleshoot issues
Less often propose overlarge patches that add risk or tech debt
More often find relevant code, instead of duplicating things
Less often “reward hack” by commenting out tests or otherwise being a dolt
Be a more effective research partner when weighing potential tech approaches
Follow our Cursor rules more diligently, including the rule not to try adding npm dependencies that don’t even flippin’ exist, you complete dingbat
Still. $1000/mo is insane. So I’ve been keeping an eye out for somebody to convince me we’re crazy.
Instead, in early June
Andrej Karpathy claimed
:
o3 is the obvious best [model] for important/hard things.
At a software company, coding counts as important. A couple days later, the Head of Engineering at Shopify
cited a coding model budget of $1k/month/dev
as being “cheap”.
Emboldened, I decided to test the water by mentioning to one of our investors – a co-founder at a relatively large tech company – that we were trialling spending $1000/mo on o3 inference.
$1000/mo! What are you doing with o3 that’s costing that much? I’m averaging $50/day on Claude Opus 4
$50/day is $1000/mo?
Oh lol right, yeah you’re good
So I guess it really is a thing. You can get $1000/mo of value from coding agents now.
How to get $1000/mo of value from coding agents
Obviously, simply spending $1000 does not guarantee you a positive return! Here are some practices that we’ve found get more value out of large thinking models like o3 and Claude Opus:
Shift errors earlier
: The faster you can detect a coding error, the cheaper it is to fix. This is doubly true for LLMs. Shifting errors from runtime → test-time → build-time makes everybody more productive. Even better, fix issues deterministically with a linter or formatter. Let your expensive LLMs and humans focus on the squishy parts.
Use boring technology

data.title: Don’t use “click here” as link text (2001)
data.author: theandrewbailey
data.article_summary: 这篇文章为网站管理员提供了关于链接文本的建议。强调不要使用“点击这里”作为链接文本，而应使用简短且有意义的文本，这些文本应在脱离上下文时仍具有信息性，解释链接内容，避免提及技术细节，且不应为动词短语。例如，避免使用“点击这里下载Amaya”，而应直接写“获取Amaya！”。文章还引用了W3C的网页内容无障碍指南和其他参考资料，强调链接文本应易读且不涉及操作细节。这些建议旨在提高网页的可访问性和用户体验。文章最后说明这些提示由W3C质量保证兴趣小组提供，仅为信息性内容，不具规范性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：链接文本的最佳实践及其对可访问性的影响

不同观点：
• **支持“点击这里”的观点**（crazygringo）：认为“点击这里”能清楚表达链接的操作性质，尤其在下载或了解更多信息的情况下，明确表示这是一个动作链接，而不是参考链接。这种用法在网络上非常普遍且有效。

• **反对“点击这里”的观点**（robin_reala, scary-size, eightnoneone, latexr）：认为“点击这里”对屏幕阅读器用户不友好，尤其是当所有链接都使用相同文本时，会剥夺这些用户通过非线性方式访问内容的便利。UK政府的数字服务指南也建议避免这种做法。

• **偏好名词链接的观点**（guhcampos, retsibsi）：倾向于使用名词或名词短语作为链接文本，认为这样更清晰地指示链接指向的内容，避免使用动词和命令语气。

• **混合观点**（zzo38computer, seanwilson）：认为在某些情况下，动词或动词短语是合适的，尤其是直接下载链接，但应确保链接文本在上下文中是有意义的。同时，可以通过技术手段为屏幕阅读器提供额外文本，以增强可访问性。

补充讨论：
• **对可访问性的进一步探讨**（jfax, smallerize）：提到一些用户难以区分页面上的不同元素，强调了网页设计中标准化和文本指示的重要性。还引用了Dragan Espenschied关于链接文本演变的文章，指出从动作指示到用户状态重配置的转变。

• **技术实现与SEO优化**（seanwilson）：强调可以通过技术手段如aria-label或CSS类来为屏幕阅读器提供额外文本，同时提高SEO效果。

• **实用性与规则的冲突**（scosman）：提到Lighthouse等工具对通用链接文本的警告，但有时这些警告会被忽略，因为一些通用文本在实际应用中仍被广泛接受。

• **对“点击这里”的技术性批评**（1970-01-01）：指出“点击这里”在触摸屏设备上的准确性问题，以及文本动态变化对用户体验的影响。

总体来看，争议焦点在于链接文本应如何平衡清晰性、可访问性和用户体验。不同用户和开发者对链接文本的最佳实践有不同的偏好和见解。

data.title: The world of Voronoi diagrams (2021)
data.author: nickcotter
data.article_summary:
Voronoi diagrams，又称Dirichlet镶嵌或Thiessen多边形，是一种将平面根据一组散点分割成若干区域的图形。每个区域包含一个点，且区域内任意位置到该点的距离比到其他点的距离更近。这种图形在自然界中非常普遍，如洋葱细胞、长颈鹿斑纹和蜂窝等。它们因能高效利用空间且在均匀生长过程中自然形成而广泛存在。

Voronoi图案还被应用于建筑和艺术中，例如2008年北京奥运会的“水立方”建筑，其外观设计灵感来源于Voronoi图。此外，中国宋代的陶瓷器物也有类似Voronoi的裂纹图案，因其独特美学价值而被推崇。

数学上，Voronoi图不仅限于二维平面，还能推广到更高维度，具有广泛的应用潜力，包括 cartography、生物学、计算机科学和统计学等领域。

44451785.article_content:
The fascinating world of Voronoi diagrams
maths
other
In this article I explain what is a Voronoi diagram and why they are amazing
Francesco S. Bellelli
07-08-2021
Voronoi diagrams
(also known as
Dirichlet tesselation
or
Thiessen polygons
) are everywhere in nature. You have encountered them thousands of times, but maybe did not call it this way. Voronoi diagram are simple, yet they have incredible properties which have found applications in fields ranging from cartography, biology, computer science, statistics, archaeology, all way to architecture and arts.
What is a Voronoi diagram?
Suppose you have
\(n\)
points scattered on a plane, the Voronoi diagram of those points subdivides the plane in exactly
\(n\)
cells enclosing the portion of the plane that is the closest to the each point. This produces a tessellation that completely covers the plane. As an illustration, in Figure 1, I plotted 100 random points and their corresponding Voronoi diagram. As you can see, every point is enclosed in a cell, whose boundaries are exactly equidistant between two or more points. In other words, all the area enclosed in the cell is closest to the point in the cell than to any other point.
Figure 1: Voronoi diagram from 100 random points in a plane
Voronoi patterns are ubiquitous
Voronoi patterns in nature
The pattern created by Voronoi diagrams is a common one in nature. In Figure 3, I made a small collage of some naturally occurring
Voronoi-like
patterns. From microscopic cells in onion skins, to the shell of jackfruits and the coat of giraffes. These patterns are everywhere!
A first reason for their omnipresence is that they form efficient shapes. As we mentioned earlier, Voronoi diagram completely tessellates the plan: hence, all space is used. This is very convenient if you are trying to squeeze as much as possible in a limited space — such as in muscle fibres or bee hives. Secondly, Voronoi diagrams are a spontaneous pattern whenever something is growing at a uniform growth rate from separate points (see Figure 2). For instance, this explains giraffe exhibit such patterns. Giraffe embryos have a scattered distribution of melanin-secreting cells, which is responsible for the dark pigmentation of the giraffe’s spots. Over the course of the gestation these cells release melanin — hence spots radiate outward. Interested reader may refer to
this paper
, in which the authors use Voronoi diagrams to model computer rendering of spots on animals coats.
Figure 2: A Voronoi diagram is obtained from constant outward growth from dispered points
Source: Wikipedia
Figure 3: Voronoi patterns are everywhere in nature.
(From top-left to bottom right: microscope view of onion skin cells, cross-section of a muscle, garlic bulb, wings of a dragonfly, soap bubbles, close-up of a leaf, giraffes coat patterns, corns, jackfruits hanging from a tree.)
Voronoi pattern in architecture and arts
Perhaps because of their spontaneous “natural” look, or simply because of their mesmerising randomness, Voronoi patterns have intentionally been implemented in human-made structures. An architectural example is the “Water cube” built to house the water sports during the 2008 Beijing Olympics. It features Voronoi diagrams on its ceiling and façades (Figure 4). The Voronoi diagrams were chosen because they recall bubbles
1
. This analogy is very clear at night, when the entire façade is illuminated in blue and comes alive.
Figure 4: Water cube in Beijing
But Chinese appreciation of Voronoi pattern is surely older than this building.
Guan
and
Ge
ware from the Song dynasty have a distinctive crackled glaze. Ceramics can easily crack during the cooling process, however the crackles from the Guan and Ge ware are different — they are intentional. They are sought after because of their aesthetic qualities, which makes each piece is unique. The forming of these patterns on the glaze is usually understood as a sequence of cracks affecting successively smaller subsets of the material’s surface. This process, known as hierarchical cracking, often yields patches of patterns similar to Voronoi diagrams. Hence, Voronoi diagram have commonly been used to
model these cracking behaviours

44451785.article_summary:
Voronoi diagrams，又称Dirichlet镶嵌或Thiessen多边形，是一种将平面根据一组散点分割成若干区域的图形。每个区域包含一个点，且区域内任意位置到该点的距离比到其他点的距离更近。这种图形在自然界中非常普遍，如洋葱细胞、长颈鹿斑纹和蜂窝等。它们因能高效利用空间且在均匀生长过程中自然形成而广泛存在。

Voronoi图案还被应用于建筑和艺术中，例如2008年北京奥运会的“水立方”建筑，其外观设计灵感来源于Voronoi图。此外，中国宋代的陶瓷器物也有类似Voronoi的裂纹图案，因其独特美学价值而被推崇。

数学上，Voronoi图不仅限于二维平面，还能推广到更高维度，具有广泛的应用潜力，包括 cartography、生物学、计算机科学和统计学等领域。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了为Intellivision游戏机开发的IntyBASIC编译器。作者在2013年10月开始开发这一项目，并在2014年1月发布了首个版本。IntyBASIC是一个跨平台编译器，能将BASIC源代码转换为Intellivision的CP1610汇编代码，支持视频和声音功能，并提供IntyColor工具用于转换BMP图像。该工具简化了游戏开发过程，受到了AtariAge社区的欢迎，并引发了新的自制游戏浪潮和编程比赛。文章还提到两本相关书籍，一本是入门教程，另一本则涵盖高级编程技巧，包括更专业的游戏开发技术。IntyBASIC适用于Windows、Mac和Linux，用户手册和最新版本可在AtariAge论坛下载。

IntyBASIC: a BASIC compiler for Intellivision
Sections:

Useful links
I was working in
Space Raid
for Intellivision when I wondered about possibilities to make easier the
development of games for Intellivision.
There is a full set of tools for emulation (
jzintv
) and
programming in assembler (as1600) created by Joseph Zbiciak (intvnut).
But in every program you need to start almost from zero
and there are few libraries.
The Intellivision console
The Intellivision being created in 1979 just around the same
time BASIC exploded as a general purpose microcomputer language, what would be
more natural than a BASIC compiler? ;)
I started working in October 2013 in my ultrasecret project
and the version 0.1 got published in January 28, 2014 with versions for
Windows, Mac and Linux.
Following the intvnut's toolset style, IntyBASIC is a cross
compiler that takes BASIC source code and translates it to CP1610 assembler
code. You only have to enter this to test your game:
intybasic game.bas game.asm
as1600 game.asm -o game
jzintv game
IntyBASIC includes support for all the Intellivision video
and sound features in form of commands like SPRITE and SOUND,
trying to be close to the hardware but so easy as possible to user.
I've keeping it updated as users and myself find bugs
or request new useful features for the compiler.
It includes also the IntyColor utility for converting BMP
images to the video format used by the Intellivision.
IntyBASIC has been pretty successful in its purpose because
the enthusiast
AtariAge
members community
and it has conducted to an explosion of new games and homebrews in the
Intellivision world and even the
IntyBASIC programming contest
.
Downloads
I suggest you to download the most recent version (v1.4.2)
from the AtariAge forums.
Latest source code of IntyBASIC and IntyColor
, sometimes with new features still not released officially.
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.4.x
(Jan/10/2019).
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.2.x
(Aug/08/2015) also check the
IntyBASIC SDK v1.1.1 for Windows
(installer including emulator/assembler).
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.1
(Jul/14/2015) also check the
IntyBASIC SDK for Windows
(installer including emulator/assembler).
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.0
(Nov/21/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.9
(Oct/10/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.8
(Aug/26/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.7
(Apr/02/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.5-v0.6
(Mar/03/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.1-v0.4
(Jan/27/2014)
The Windows version of IntyBASIC works since XP, but if
your version doesn't have service packs it could need the
Visual C++ 2008 runtime
.
If you're using Mac, you need Mac OS X v10.6 or better. In
case of Linux, any recent version should work.
The user's manual is included inside the ZIP file.
I suggest strongly to register in AtariAge where you can
get help on using IntyBASIC just by reading the
Intellivision Programming
forum or posting your questions.
The book
The success of IntyBASIC inspired me to write a book called "Programming Games for Intellivision".
It follows the learning technique that was so useful for me when starting in the BASIC language: Games published in parts,
required to be typed by hand, and detailed explanation of each part.
The book has 192 pages, and is available both in paperback and hardcover:
Hardcover from
Lulu.com
and
Amazon.com
.
Paperback from
Lulu.com
and
Amazon.com
.
Also available as
ebook from my digital store
.
Check the reviews by
The No Swear Gamer
and a cool hands-on review by
Gray Defender
.
Advanced Game Programming for Intellivision
Inspired by the success of my first book, I went to write another book including more advanced techniques of programming. In particular I wanted to explore the development of games looking more professional both on terms of title screens, gameplay, sound, and music.
The complete source code for Oh Mummy! Pumpkin Master, Meteor Storm, and Dungeon Warrior is included. Each of these games includes a particular technique that I wanted to comment: Oh Mummy! movement of the player on a maze, and how enemies pursue the player. Pumpkin Master, shooters techniques to create tons of bullets without exceeding total sprites. Meteor Storm, techniques for pseudo-3D scaling of sprites, animation of screen zones with multiple images. Dungeon Warrior, techniques for drawing pseudo-3D mazes on screen, including scaling of enemies per depth, and of course algorithms for Role Playing Games.
A full chapter dedicated to the creation of sound effects and converting music sheets to IntyBASIC is included, furthermore tips for converting pictures to Intellivision graphics.
The book has 294 pages, and is available in paperback: (Soon in hardcover)

ebook from my digital store
.

npm install --save-dev @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor

data.title: The uv build back end is now stable
data.author: NeutralForest
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了**uv build backend**的功能和使用方法。它是用于将源代码目录构建为Python源码分发包或wheel的工具，目前默认后端为**hatchling**，但未来将改为**uv**。  
**uv build backend**支持所有符合**PEP 517**的构建后端，同时提供原生的**uv_build**后端，以提高性能和用户体验。它具有零配置的合理默认值，但也可以灵活配置以适应不同项目结构，且能验证项目元数据，防止常见错误。  
当前，**uv build backend**仅支持纯Python代码，若项目包含扩展模块，需使用其他后端。要使用**uv_build**后端，需在**pyproject.toml**中指定，并可通过**uv init**创建新项目。  
**uv**可捆绑**uv_build**后端，但也可独立安装。此外，文章还介绍了模块、命名空间包、存根包的处理方式及文件包含与排除的配置方法。

The uv build backend
Note
Currently, the default build backend for
uv init
is
hatchling
. This will change to
uv
in a future version.
A build backend transforms a source tree (i.e., a directory) into a source distribution or a wheel.
uv supports all build backends (as specified by
PEP 517
), but
also provides a native build backend (
uv_build
) that integrates tightly with uv to improve
performance and user experience.
Choosing a build backend
The uv build backend is a great choice for most Python projects. It has reasonable defaults, with
the goal of requiring zero configuration for most users, but provides flexible configuration to
accommodate most Python project structures. It integrates tightly with uv, to improve messaging and
user experience. It validates project metadata and structures, preventing common mistakes. And,
finally, it's very fast.
The uv build backend currently
only supports pure Python code
. An alternative backend is
required to build a
library with extension modules
.
Tip
While the backend supports a number of options for configuring your project structure, when build scripts or
a more flexible project layout are required, consider using the
hatchling
build backend instead.
Using the uv build backend
To use uv as a build backend in an existing project, add
uv_build
to the
[build-system]
section in your
pyproject.toml
:
pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires
=
[
"uv_build>=0.7.19,<0.8.0"
]
build-backend
=
"uv_build"
Note
The uv build backend follows the same
versioning policy
as uv. Including an upper bound on the
uv_build
version ensures that your package continues to
build correctly as new versions are released.
To create a new project that uses the uv build backend, use
uv init
:
$
uv
init
--build-backend
uv
When the project is built, e.g., with
uv build
, the uv build backend will
be used to create the source distribution and wheel.
Bundled build backend
The build backend is published as a separate package (
uv_build
) that is optimized for portability
and small binary size. However, the
uv
executable also includes a copy of the build backend, which
will be used during builds performed by uv, e.g., during
uv build
, if its version is compatible
with the
uv_build
requirement. If it's not compatible, a compatible version of the
uv_build
package will be used. Other build frontends, such as
python -m build
, will always use the
uv_build
package, typically choosing the latest compatible version.
Modules
Python packages are expected to contain one or more Python modules, which are directories containing
an
__init__.py
. By default, a single root module is expected at
src/<package_name>/__init__.py
.
For example, the structure for a project named
foo
would be:
pyproject.toml
src
└── foo
└── __init__.py
uv normalizes the package name to determine the default module name: the package name is lowercased
and dots and dashes are replaced with underscores, e.g.,
Foo-Bar
would be converted to
foo_bar
.
The
src/
directory is the default directory for module discovery.
These defaults can be changed with the
module-name
and
module-root
settings. For example, to use
a
FOO
module in the root directory, as in the project structure:
pyproject.toml
FOO
└── __init__.py
The correct build configuration would be:
pyproject.toml
[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name
=
"FOO"
module-root
=
""
Namespace packages
Namespace packages are intended for use-cases where multiple packages write modules into a shared
namespace.
Namespace package modules are identified by a
.
in the
module-name
. For example, to package the
module
bar
in the shared namespace
foo
, the project structure would be:
pyproject.toml
src
└── foo
└── bar
└── __init__.py
And the
module-name
configuration would be:
pyproject.toml
[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name
=
"foo.bar"
Important
The
__init__.py
file is not included in
foo
, since it's the shared namespace module.
It's also possible to have a complex namespace package with more than one root module, e.g., with
the project structure:
pyproject.toml
src
├── foo
│   └── __init__.py
└── bar
└── __init__.py
While we do not recommend this structure (i.e., you should use a workspace with multiple packages
instead), it is supported via the
namespace
option:
pyproject.toml
[tool.uv.build-backend]
namespace
=
true
Stub packages
The build backend also supports building type stub packages, which are identified by the
-stubs
suffix on the package or module name, e.g.,
foo-stubs
. The module name for type stub packages must
end in
-stubs
, so uv will not normalize the
-
to an underscore. Additionally, uv will search for
a
__init__.pyi
file. For example, the project structure would be:
pyproject.toml
src
└── foo-stubs
└── __init__.pyi
Type stub modules are also supported for
namespace packages
.
File inclusion and exclusion
The build backend is responsible for determining which files in a source tree should be packaged
into the distributions.

data.title: Opening up ‘Zero-Knowledge Proof’ technology
data.author: doomroot13
data.article_summary: 谷歌开源了其零知识证明（ZKP）库，以增强隐私保护，特别是在年龄验证方面。ZKP技术允许用户证明某些信息为真，而无需分享其他数据，例如在不需要透露其他信息的情况下证明自己年满18岁。通过开放这些加密工具的源代码，谷歌旨在帮助公共和私营部门的开发者构建更注重隐私的应用和数字身份解决方案。这不仅有利于用户享有更私密和安全的数字环境，还帮助企业和研究人员满足隐私需求并开发新应用。此举也响应了欧盟即将于2026年生效的eIDAS法规，鼓励成员国在欧洲数字身份钱包中采用增强隐私的技术。源代码可在GitHub上获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非交互式零知识证明（Zero-Knowledge Proofs, ZKPs）的直觉解释及其应用

不同观点：
• **对非交互式零知识证明的直观理解需求**：[bobbiechen] 提到对交互式零知识证明有较好的理解，但难以找到对非交互式零知识证明的直观解释，并提供了一些参考资料。
• **隐私与身份验证的应用**：[natch] 认为零知识证明可以在保护隐私的前提下解决许多因过度分享个人信息（PII）导致的问题，例如使用社会保障号码（SSNs）。
• **技术实现与安全性争议**：[csense] 提出如何防御通过未经授权的方式获取私钥并绕过验证手段的攻击。

补充讨论：
• **零知识证明的历史与商业化**：[ChuckMcM] 回顾了零知识证明技术在90年代的商业化尝试，如DigiCash和Andy Birrell的微支付概念，并表达了对这些技术重新应用的兴趣。
• **复杂性与应用限制**：[Confiks] 讨论了一种复杂的多展示无关性与硬件绑定的解决方案，指出其复杂性和应用限制，并提到绕过验证的潜在方法。
• **去中心化身份验证的潜力**：[esbranson] 认为零知识证明可以用于去中心化身份验证，例如在不提供个人信息的情况下验证政治党派 affiliation。
• **技术扩展与应用场景**：[est] 询问是否可以通过零知识证明验证电子邮件地址的有效性。[vvpan] 提到 zkTLS 技术可以在不透露用户名的情况下证明拥有某个在线服务的账户。

争议焦点：
• **隐私保护与绕过验证的可能性**：[Confiks] 与 [csense] 都提到即使有隐私保护机制，验证系统仍可能被绕过，强调需要设定合理的期望。
• **技术的创新性与实用性**：[hrdwdmrbl] 质疑该技术是否在当前研究前沿仍具有创新性和实用性，或者已经被其他团队超越。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **具体应用场景的讨论**：[Labo333] 提到在法国和美国一些州，成人内容网站因难以实现年龄验证而受到影响。[baby] 分享了关于零知识证明的资讯平台。[mumbisChungo] 提到零知识证明在分布式网络中保护信息隐私的应用。[ranger_danger] 质疑零知识证明如何验证请求来自真人而非机器人。
• **潜在商业应用**：[cyberax] 提出该技术可能实现类似Scroll的匿名付费浏览网络。

总结：讨论主要围绕非交互式零知识证明的直观理解、技术实现与安全性、隐私保护与绕过验证的可能性、以及该技术在不同场景下的应用潜力与限制。

Opening up ‘Zero-Knowledge Proof’ technology to promote privacy in age assurance
Jul 03, 2025
·
Share
Twitter

Alan Stapelberg
Group Product Manager, Google Wallet
Share

Copy link
Today, we open sourced our
Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) libraries
, fulfilling a
promise
and building on our
partnership with Sparkasse
to support
EU age assurance
.
Open sourcing these powerful cryptographic tools will make it much easier for private and public sector developers to build their own privacy-enhancing applications and digital ID solutions, meeting an urgent need.
In layperson’s terms, ZKP makes it possible for people to prove that something about them is
true
without exchanging any other data. So, for example, a person visiting a website can verifiably prove he or she is over 18, without sharing anything else at all.
The goal of sharing ZKP with the open source and cryptography communities reflects our commitment to helping
all
parties in the ecosystem:
Web and app users benefit from being inhabitants of a more private and secure digital ecosystem.
Businesses and other relying organizations of all sizes can easily leverage this open source solution to meet their privacy needs.
Developers can freely use the ZKP codebase to build privacy-focused applications.
Researchers can use this more efficient and performant ZKP implementation to help create new applications and uses of technology.
The European Union’s eIDAS Regulation set to take effect in 2026 encourages Member States to integrate privacy-enhancing technologies like ZKP into the European Digital Identity Wallet (“EUDI Wallet”). With our commitment to making these ZKP tools openly available, Member States can integrate this into their future EUDI Wallets, accelerating their development.
We're so excited for this new chapter for Zero-Knowledge Proofs and invite you to explore the ZKP codebase on
https://github.com/google/longfellow-zk
.

• **对双足机器人稳定性的担忧**：BrandiATMuhkuh 基于过去的实验经验，认为双足机器人存在稳定性差、漂移严重的问题，并质疑选择双足而非四足设计的原因。这反映了对双足机器人实际应用中的技术瓶颈的担忧。

• **对机器人脚部设计的讨论**：chrsw 提出为什么大多数 humanoid 机器人没有类似人类足部的关节（如跖趾关节），并指出人类足部的柔性和神经末梢对机器人移动性能的重要性。这涉及对机器人仿生设计和硬件局限性的讨论。

• **对全自主机器人的算法和市场质疑**：randomNumber7 质疑项目方在全自主机器人中使用的机器学习算法，并指出硬件易得、控制难，特别是如何吸引开发者贡献开源代码。同时，也表达了对市场前景的担忧，认为消费者不一定会为开源代码买单。

• **对市场定位和消费动机的分析**：v5v3 认为当前购买人形机器人的消费者多出于对“女性形象”机器人的兴趣，而非功能性需求。这指向了一个较为细分甚至带有性别刻板印象的消费市场。

• **对市场需求和融资策略的讨论**：markisus 提出该项目面临“为技术找应用场景”的问题，并质疑其市场潜力。同时，对项目如何获得投资表示好奇。这反映了技术创业中常见的市场不确定性问题。

• **对价格和实际应用的讨论**：deepdarkforest 认为当前人形机器人实用性不足，并质疑项目方在未完全实现自主功能前的高价销售策略。这与 ZeroCool2u 对价格的积极评价形成对比，表明消费者对价格和实际功能的敏感度不同。

补充讨论：
• **对机器人硬件和软件开发的平衡**：accurrent 和 dbmikus 都提到了与现有竞争对手（如中国的 Unitree）的比较，关注项目方在硬件和软件开发上的资源分配，尤其是如何在市场竞争中取得优势。

• **对机器人手部设计的期待**：lachyg 关注机器人手部的设计，询问何时能出现价格合理且性能可靠的多指机械手，反映了业界对精细操作能力的需求。

• **对不同配置和升级的疑问**：dan344 和 fragmede 都对机器人不同配置的价格和性能差异提出疑问，特别是 $3000 的差价包含哪些额外功能，这涉及消费者对产品性价比的关注。

• **对开源项目的实际参与**：pj_mukh 表示没有足够时间和预算参与硬件开发，但希望了解项目中开放的软件问题，显示了对开源项目不同参与程度的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• **双足设计的可行性和市场定位**：部分讨论者质疑双足设计的实际效果和市场需求，认为四足或其他设计可能更稳定和实用。
• **高价与功能性不匹配**：一些评论者认为当前人形机器人在未完全实现自主功能的情况下，售价过高，难以吸引广泛市场。

总结：讨论围绕技术实现、市场需求、价格策略和消费者动机展开，显示了人形机器人在技术、市场和消费层面的多重挑战。

data.title: EBAF – eBPF Based Ad Firewall
data.author: ARob109
data.article_summary: eBAF（eBPF Ad Firewall）是一个开源广告拦截工具，专门用于阻止Spotify等平台的广告。它通过eBPF技术在 kernel 层面过滤网络数据包，利用黑名单阻止广告相关的IP地址，并支持动态更新以应对变化的广告服务器。该工具提供高效、透明且易用的广告拦截方案，通过提供实时统计和监控的网页控制面板，用户可以直观地查看拦截效果。eBAF直接在网络接口层面操作，绕过内核网络堆栈，以实现高性能和低资源占用。该项目不仅是为了跳过烦人的广告，更是为了抵制将用户注意力商品化的系统，强调阻止广告不是盗窃，而是一种数字抵抗行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用技术手段屏蔽Spotify广告以及是否构成盗版的争议

不同观点：
• Retr0id：最初怀疑横幅图是AI生成，经过对比细节和检查元数据后发现确实是AI生成，并提到OpenAI通过元数据对图像输出进行水印标记。
• mfro：认为没有必要进行内核级别的包过滤，可以使用更简单的方法如修改host文件或自建DNS服务器。同时批评项目试图修改用户的sudoers文件，认为这是一个糟糕的项目。
• bobbyraduloff：认为使用内核级别手段屏蔽Spotify广告类似于使用GPT生成的道德辩护。指出用户没有权利要求免费音乐服务，如果不满意Spotify的条款，可以选择其他服务或直接购买音乐。批评以“不满意服务价值”为借口进行盗版是不合理的。
• _benj：质疑这种方法与IP或DNS广告屏蔽器的区别，认为都是基于黑名单，并提出eBPF可能会增加复杂性。
• sbarre：认为如果不喜欢Spotify，可以选择不使用，而不是试图通过技术手段屏蔽广告。批评项目开发者的道德辩护是幼稚的，并指出这种行为实际上是盗窃。
• sciencesama：建议将该技术扩展到其他平台如Reddit、Facebook和Instagram的广告屏蔽，使用代理实现。
• alephnerd：对该技术与eBPF的共存能力表示关注，提到如果使用像Crowdstrike这样的XDR，可能会干扰其在Linux桌面上的eBPF传感器。
• jekwoooooe：认为这种行为是盗 piracy，不论项目开发者如何否认，因为免费Spotify的协议就是通过广告支持服务。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于使用技术手段屏蔽Spotify广告是否构成盗 piracy。
• 讨论还涉及技术实现的复杂性和合理性，如内核级别过滤的必要性以及eBPF的应用可能带来的问题。
• 有人提出道德和法律层面的批评，认为这种行为是不道德的，并且可能面临法律风险如DMCA下架。

eBAF - eBPF Based Ad Firewall
"You Wouldn't Download an Ad"
But You Would Block One!
Spotify has built an empire on a simple formula: monetize your attention, underpay the artists, and sell you back your own time as a premium feature.
In their world, your listening experience is not yours. It’s a carefully curated marketplace — your ears are the product, your patience is the currency.
They like to call it a "free" tier.
But let’s be honest: it’s not free if you’re paying with your time.
Meanwhile, the artists you love — the people whose work keeps the platform alive — often earn mere fractions of pennies per stream. Spotify profits handsomely, the advertisers get their exposure, and the creators? They get scraps.
This isn’t just about skipping a few annoying ads.
It’s about refusing to participate in a system that profits from exploitation, distraction, and the commodification of your attention.
What is this?
An elegant little act of digital resistance: a clean, open-source adblocker for Spotify that stops the noise — literally.
No sketchy mods, no cracked clients, no malware masquerading as freedom. Just one goal: let the music play without being held hostage by ads.
Spotify isn’t free — you pay with your patience.
They bombard you with the same grating ads, over and over, until you give up and subscribe. Not because you love Premium. But because you’ve been worn down. That’s not freemium — that’s psychological warfare with a playlist.
Meanwhile, the artists? Still underpaid.
The ads? Louder. More frequent. Sometimes literally louder.
You? Just trying to vibe.
They profit from your patience and their underpayment of creators, all while pretending it’s the only sustainable way. Spoiler: it isn’t. They had a choice — but they chose profit margins over people.
Spotify wants you to believe this is the cost of access.
We believe that’s a lie.
We’re not pirates. We’re not criminals. We’re just people who think it's okay to draw a line.
This project isn’t about skipping a few ads. It’s about rejecting a system that says your silence can be sold, your experience can be interrupted, and your value begins only when you open your wallet.
Blocking ads is not theft.
Stealing your time is.
We’re not here to pirate. We’re here to opt out.
You wouldnt Download an Ad. But you would block one.
How does eBAF work?
eBAF (eBPF Ad Firewall) leverages the power of eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) to block unwanted advertisements at the kernel level. Here's a high-level overview of its functionality:
How does eBAF work?
eBAF (eBPF Ad Firewall) leverages eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) to block ads at the kernel level efficiently. Here's a simplified overview:
Packet Filtering
:
Inspects incoming network packets and blocks those matching a blacklist of IP addresses using XDP (eXpress Data Path).
Dynamic Updates
:
Resolves domain names into IP addresses and updates the blacklist dynamically to stay effective against changing ad servers.
Web Dashboard
:
Provides live statistics and monitoring through a user-friendly interface.
High Performance
:
Operates directly at the network interface level, bypassing the kernel's networking stack for faster processing and minimal resource usage.
eBAF combines efficiency, transparency, and ease of use to deliver a powerful ad-blocking solution.
Simple Install (Reccomended)
Make sure to have git and curl installed
git --version
curl --version
Install
Enable Spotify integration (Recommended)
EBAF_ENABLE_SPOTIFY=yes curl -sSL https://github.com/Kazedaa/eBAF/raw/main/install.sh
|
sudo -E bash
Disable explicitly
EBAF_ENABLE_SPOTIFY=no curl -sSL https://github.com/Kazedaa/eBAF/raw/main/install.sh
|
sudo bash
`
`
`
Uninstall
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kazedaa/eBAF/main/uninstall.sh
|
sudo bash
Dev Install
Run the following commands to install the required dependencies:
Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install libbpf-dev clang llvm libelf-dev zlib1g-dev gcc make python3
sudo apt update
sudo apt install net-tools
Fedora/CentOS/RHEL 8+
sudo dnf update
sudo dnf install -y libbpf-devel clang llvm elfutils-libelf-devel zlib-devel gcc make python3 net-tools bc
Arch
sudo pacman -Syu
sudo pacman -S --needed libbpf clang llvm libelf zlib gcc m

data.title: AV1@Scale: Film Grain Synthesis, The Awakening
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: Netflix最新博文介绍了AV1编解码器中的胶片颗粒合成（Film Grain Synthesis, FGS）技术，该技术旨在优化流媒体视频的视觉质量和压缩效率。胶片颗粒为影片增添了真实感和怀旧感，但其随机性给视频压缩带来了挑战。AV1通过使用自回归模型（AR模型）捕捉颗粒图案，并通过缩放函数调整颗粒强度，从而在保留艺术完整性的同时实现高效压缩。FGS技术首先对视频进行去噪，然后压缩视频，并在播放时重新合成胶片颗粒。这不仅提升了画质，还显著减少了比特率，为用户提供了更流畅的高质量观影体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电影噪点（grain）的保留、去除与合成对视频质量和观看体验的影响

不同观点：
• crazygringo：认为合成噪点无法还原原始噪点中的细节，实际视频对比静止图像更能看出细节保留或丢失的区别。如果编码不考虑多帧信息，直接帧对帧去噪并合成，会导致模糊的观看体验。
• fidotron：指出评论中的去噪过程过度模糊，且合成的噪点不像真正的胶片颗粒，导致图像不够锐利。
• jedbrooke：不认同噪点等同于现实主义，但承认噪点作为艺术工具的作用，认为技术本身仍具有价值。
• derf_：强调噪点合成技术在AV1编码器中早已存在，但此前需要手动调整，现在更广泛的应用是技术进步，不过缺乏具体技术细节。
• dperfect：认为噪点和颗粒自然存在，能增加感知锐度并掩盖缺陷，如色带和压缩伪影。尽管不是所有噪点都有益，但去噪后的平滑效果更不现实且分散注意力。
• supertrope：通过手机通话编码的例子说明合成噪点在某些情况下比完全没有噪点更好。
• eviks：反对噪点，认为它只是视觉噪音，遮挡了真实场景的细节，且噪点与现实无关，更支持去噪并提供关闭选项。
• _bent：对先去噪再加噪的处理流程感到不满，认为这是不必要的复杂化。
• vessenes：支持噪点合成技术，认为能以较低比特率接近原始影片效果，尤其对老影片有意义。
• smusamashah：认为原始噪点是数据而非随机噪音，能通过提取噪点还原场景细节，类比图像抖动技术。
• jrm4：认为任何明显的“瑕疵”最终都会成为一种美学选择，对噪点成为审美选择表示有趣。
• UltraSane：批评对24帧率和胶片噪点的过度依赖，认为这是落后的技术。
• dudeinjapan：调侃建议给音频也加上噪音。
• vachina：讽刺创新枯竭。
• ConanRus：希望使用完全不压缩的原始胶片扫描，拒绝任何损失细节的技术，如JPEG压缩。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于噪点是否为细节的一部分，一些人认为噪点增加了深度和真实感，而另一些人认为噪点是视觉噪音，遮挡了真实细节。
- 技术实现的讨论中，涉及去噪和噪点合成算法如何影响视频质量，尤其是对老电影的修复和现代编码的应用。
- 对合成噪点的审美和技术价值存在不同看法，部分人认为它是艺术表现的一部分，而另一些人则希望完全去除。

AV1 @ Scale: Film Grain Synthesis, The Awakening
Unleashing Film Grain Synthesis on Netflix and Enhancing Visuals for Millions
Netflix Technology Blog

Li-Heng Chen
